originalTitle: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Monday
simplifiedContent: Here's a simple explanation of the news: The Indian stock market has been going down for five days in a row, partly because oil prices are high and foreign investors are selling their shares. Even though the market tried to bounce back a bit, people are still feeling negative about it due to rising interest rates in the US and uncertainty around the world. This means that investors are being cautious and watching what happens next. Analysts are keeping an eye on certain important levels that the market might reach, which could affect how it moves on Monday. This will help determine how the market will perform tomorrow.

originalTitle: US Fed action, oil swings to test bullion as traders eye West Asia risks: Analysts
simplifiedContent: This is an important week for gold and silver prices because the US Federal Reserve is going to make a decision about interest rates. What they decide will likely affect the prices of these metals. At the same time, changes in oil prices and rising tensions between the US and Iran are also expected to impact gold and silver prices. Additionally, some key economic reports and announcements from central banks will also play a role in determining the prices of these metals. This means that traders are watching many different factors that could cause gold and silver prices to go up or down.

originalTitle: GS, Nomura, Axis hired to run Carlyle’s India automotive platform IPO
simplifiedContent: Carlyle, a big investment company, is planning to sell part of its stake in an Indian auto-parts business called Highway Roop Precision Technologies. To do this, they're working with several big banks, including GS, Nomura, and Axis, to help sell the company's shares to the public in an Initial Public Offering (IPO). The IPO is expected to raise $500 million, and could value the entire company at $2 billion. This matters because it's a way for Carlyle to make money from its investment in the company. By selling some of its shares, Carlyle is giving other investors a chance to own a part of the company.

originalTitle: CBDT issues crypto asset reporting guidelines for exchanges under Income-tax Act 2025
simplifiedContent: The government's tax department, known as the CBDT, has created rules for cryptocurrency exchanges to follow when reporting information. This is part of a bigger plan to share tax information internationally, which has been supported by a group of 20 important countries (called the G20). The rules are part of a new law called the Income-tax Act 2025. This matters because it will help the government keep track of cryptocurrency transactions and make sure people are paying the right amount of taxes. The goal is to improve how tax information is shared between countries, which will help prevent tax evasion.

originalTitle: Wall St Week Ahead-US stocks face tests from Fed decision, tech-led earnings deluge
simplifiedContent: This week, the US stock market will be closely watched as two major events happen. The Federal Reserve (or "Fed") will make a decision that could affect the market, and many big technology companies will release their earnings reports. These reports will show how well these companies have done financially, which can impact their stock prices. This is important because it can help investors decide whether to buy or sell stocks, and how the overall market might perform. The combination of the Fed's decision and the earnings reports will be a big test for the US stock market.

originalTitle: Expert View: Mid-year - recalibrating India equity story with a positive bias, says Vinod Nair
simplifiedContent: An expert named Vinod Nair is sharing his thoughts on the Indian stock market. He believes that the market will do well, with a positive outlook, as we reach the middle of the year. He thinks that the market will keep going up, and has set a target of 29,000 for December 2027. This means he expects the market to increase by 21% over the next few years, which could be a good sign for investors. This prediction matters because it could help investors make informed decisions about where to put their money.
